subject: Week 16: 4-month well visit opens Monday; five vaccines due
bodyText:
This week
The 4-month well visit window opens Monday, Aug 31 — the pediatrician will run the full CDC 4-month checklist (https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html): smiling for attention, chuckling, cooing back at you, holding his head steady unsupported, pushing up on forearms, swinging at toys. Expect the sleep regression on the agenda whether you raise it or not. Worth asking there: early allergen introduction at 4 months vs. solids at six, growth trajectory, and iron status if exclusively breastfeeding.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Extensive drooling and hand-mouthing — salivary maturation precedes first teeth (typically 6–10 months) by 2–3 months.
- [monitor] A persistent flat spot or head asymmetry — the pediatrician may discuss a helmet referral around 6 months if it is not improving.
- [call within 24h] Post-vaccine injection-site reaction with a hard knot over 2 inches, new-onset feeding refusal, or persistent vomiting.
- [call now] Fever ≥102°F rectal, seizure activity, or anaphylaxis signs after vaccines (hives with breathing difficulty, facial swelling) — 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Get the SFPL library card if you have not and put one weekly Baby Rhyme & Play Time on the standing calendar — free, runs infants to 15 months, ticketed same-day at popular branches. The Cantonese and Spanish storytimes double as free live second-language exposure blocks. SFPL Baby Rhyme & Play Time: https://sfpl.org/kids/kids/events/storytime-sfpl
- Tour Montessori nidos and join waitlists now if a nido is the childcare plan: Cosmos Montessori SF takes 3–12-month-olds with a 3-child cap, so capacity is effectively the waitlist. Evaluate it as premium-ratio childcare — no outcome study supports a Montessori-specific effect under 12 months. Cosmos Montessori SF nido: https://www.cosmosmontessorisf.com/program-3
- Settle the solids philosophy question — baby-led weaning vs. purées — and order the high chair this week, even on a 6-month timeline; Monday's visit is the right venue for the early-allergen question. AAP: Starting Solid Foods: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/feeding-nutrition/Pages/Starting-Solid-Foods.aspx
- Hold a toy within batting range and let him swing, grab, and bring it to his mouth — the exact skills on the checklist he will be assessed against.

Upcoming
- Day 112–126 (Aug 31–Sep 14, 2026): 4-month well visit; vaccines: RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2. Dose acetaminophen weight-based and only after symptoms appear — prophylactic dosing blunts the antibody response.
- Day 117 (Sep 5, 2026): next email — post-vaccine recovery and the sleep-training one-week check.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses arm to swing at hanging toys
  AAP window: day 90-150
  What to look for: Pre-reaching swiping — not yet visually-guided grasp.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/swings-at-toys/complete

- Laughs out loud
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Full belly laugh, not just a smile with sound. Often triggered by gentle physical play or peekaboo.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/laughs/complete

- Reaches to grab a toy he wants
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Visually-guided reaching, eye-hand coordination.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/reaches-for-toy/complete

- Rolls from tummy to back
  AAP window: day 90-180
  What to look for: Usually appears first — back-to-tummy follows later. Once rolling begins, stop swaddling for sleep.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/6-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/rolls-tummy-to-back/complete

- Looks at you, moves, or makes sounds to keep your attention
  AAP window: day 70-120
  What to look for: Active engagement — baby is now driving the interaction, not just responding.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/4-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-to-get-attention/complete
